Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to start Day 4! We can see the South African opening pair, Edward Moore and Neil Brand walk out to the middle now. So, that means New Zealand have declared, and the target for the Proteas will be 529 runs. The conditions are a bit overcast which will help the pacers which makes their task even more difficult. Tim Southee has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

New Zealand faced an early setback with the dismissal of Tom Latham, who once again fell for a low score. However, Kane Williamson and Devon Conway stitched a superb 92-run partnership, putting the tourists under pressure. After Conway's departure for 29, Rachin Ravindra, the double centurion from the first innings, too couldn't stay long at the crease and fell for just 12. Nevertheless, the veteran Kane Williamson notched up another century, became the fifth Kiwi player to score a century in both innings and helped to consolidate New Zealand's position in the game. Daryl Mitchell and Tom Blundell negotiated the end of the day's play and will look to add more runs in the first session. Neil Brand, the Proteas' skipper, managed to pick up two wickets, supported by Ruan de Swardt and Dane Paterson with one each. However, their efforts don't reflect much progress at this stage. With a substantial deficit of 528 runs already, South Africa find themselves in dire straits, needing more than a miracle to turn the tide, a task that seems next to impossible. The first session of Day 4 is just around the corner. Stay tuned.

Hello and a very warm welcome to our coverage of Day 4 of this highly anticipated first Test between New Zealand and South Africa from Bay Oval, Mount Maunganui. The hosts have asserted their dominance over the first three days, firmly controlling the match. New Zealand managed to dismiss South Africa for a mere 162 runs, with Mitchell Santner and Matt Henry taking three wickets each, while Kyle Jamieson and Rachin Ravindra chipped in with two wickets apiece. Keegan Petersen fought a lone battle amidst the collapse, only to be eventually undone by Ravindra's solid bowling. The Kiwi bowlers prevented any significant partnerships from developing, granting them a commanding lead of 342 runs. The hosts didn't impose the follow-on to ensure that the hosts don't creep back into the contest.
...DAY 4, FIRST SESSION...

Right then, that is it from Day 3 of this first Test which was completely dominated by New Zealand and South Africa are in all sorts of trouble now. We will have to wait and see if Tim Southee declares before the start of Day 4 or if the Kiwis bat a bit longer. The fourth Day will begin on 7th February, Wednesday at 3.30 am IST (10 pm GMT, Previous Day), but you can join use early for all the build-up. Cheers!

Devon Conway and Kane Williamson looked pretty good after Tea and continued to tire out the bowlers and racked up the runs too. Towards the end of the session, the message was pretty clear as the batters started going for big shots. Devon Conway holed out while Rachin Ravindra also went back trying to be aggressive. Williamson held one end strongly and went on to register a brilliant ton. However, he was dismissed as well trying to attack the bowlers. Neil Brand picked up a couple of wickets in the final session while Ruan de Swardt got one as well. The way the Kiwis ended the session, and with a huge lead 528 runs, it doesn't look likely that they will come out to bat again on Day 4.

In the second session, the only set batter, Keegan Petersen who looked solid from the start tried to build up partnerships, but got no real support. He ultimately lost his patience and gave away his wicket, and their tail couldn't really wag much as they were bowled out for 162. The Kiwi spin duo of Mitchell Santner and Rachin Ravindra shared the last five Proteas wickets. While batting, Tom Latham went back for another low score, and Devon Conway and Kane Williamson saw out till Tea. Dane Paterson was the lone wicket-taker for Proteas in that session while Tshepo Moreki bowled well but did not have anything to show for it.

The Kiwi bowlers were right on the money from the start of Day 3. They put the pressure on the batters and made them make mistakes. Matt Henry started things off with a double-wicket over while Mitchell Santner followed it with one as well as he was getting a lot of turn. They did not concede too many runs and got into a commanding position before Lunch. The Proteas batters went completely into defensive mode, and there was not much intent to score runs which did not help either as they ended the first session with seven wickets down.

SESSION SUMMARY - 152 runs and 3 wickets in 33 overs! The Kiwis are way ahead in this Test now! Day 3 is called the 'Moving Day' and this has surely moved in the way of the hosts. The highlight was obviously that exceptional hundred from Kane Williamson as he went back-to-back in this Test. South Africa, whenever they do come out to bat will need to register the highest successful chase in Test history to win this game.
Fuller in length and angling into the leg stump from the middle, Tom Blundell flicks it to deep mid-wicket for a single. And this wraps up the Day 3 of the first Test.

OUT! STUMPED! Kane Williamson departs on a well-made 109! Sees him charging ahead does Neil Brand and fires in a length on the stump line, it keeps straight after pitching, Kane Williamson anticipates for the ball to turn a bit but misses to heave it over the deep mid-wicket region but plays it completely down the wrong line, and the ball sneaks through the gap between the bat and the pad. The keeper collects it and comfortably breaks the stumps. Kane Williamson is stranded way outside the crease. Neil Brand gets his man but this has been an exceptional innings from the former Kiwi skipper. Back-to-back centuries from him and he has troubled and tired the Proteas bowlers to say the least.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the final session of Day 3 to begin. Approx 33 overs to be bowled in this session. The two Umpires are already out in the middle. South African fielders take their respective field positions. Kane Williamson and Devon Conway stroll out to resume their innings. Ruan de Swardt will be bowling the first over post-Tea break. Let's play...
...DAY 3, THIRD SESSION...

SESSION SUMMARY - 60 runs and 4 wickets in 26.5 overs! Another Kiwi-dominated session! The spin duo of Mitchell Santner and Rachin Ravindra was looking threatening before Lunch joined hands and shared the last three wickets to bowl out the Proteas in an hour or so. New Zealand had the opportunity to enforce follow-on but decided against it. They came out to bat with a 349-run lead, but lost Tom Latham to Dane Paterson early on. Devon Conway struggled a bit initially but was able to see out the rest of the session along with Kane Williamson and extended the lead to 376 runs. The Proteas pacers, Dane Paterson and Tshepo Moreki were decent but only have one wicket to show. They will be hoping to pick up a few wickets before Stumps, while it will be interesting to see when the Kiwis invite the Proteas for the chase. Join us at 8.30 pm IST (3 am GMT) for all the action in the last session.
On a good length just around off, Kane Williamson waits for it on the back foot before cutting it away to backward point for a single. And that will be Tea on Day 3.
